answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can use unpredictable live checkpoints. Each identity is a kernel that must stay responsive: the network sends short prompts at random, as at a wharf. Prompt answers prove a real operator behind it; missing several checkpoints freezes rewards. One operator cannot staff dozens of identities at once, because checkpoints overlap and cannot be precomputed. Hiring stand-ins means paying a full wage per fake agent; cost grows per identity, gain stays flat, so mass forgery stops paying. Genuine attention, like jade, is hard to fake at scale.
